title: UFO Investigator Allegedly Concludes Aliens Are Actually Demonic Spirits After Hearing Jesus Calls
excerpt: UFO investigator Joe Jordan says alleged abduction accounts ending after appeals to Jesus shaped his belief that some encounters are spiritual.
content:
Florida-based UFO investigator Joe Jordan says testimony from people who reported frightening alien-abduction experiences helped shape his belief that some such encounters may be spiritual rather than extraterrestrial.

Jordan, 72, is president and co-founder of the CE4 Research Group and has said he has investigated UFO reports since the early 1990s.

He has also described himself as a safety professional working for Blue Origin in Florida. His UFO research is separate from his employment.

Jordan says his Christian faith began in 1996, before much of the case material he later collected. In a July 2026 interview, he said he had worked with 'well over 700' case histories since 1997 involving people who reported alleged abduction experiences.

UFO Investigator Says Witnesses Reported Experiences Ending After Prayers

Jordan said one case involving a man identified only as 'Bill D' changed the direction of his research. According to Jordan's account, the man described a frightening experience that he interpreted as satanic and said he cried out, 'Jesus, Jesus, help me!' before the episode ended.

Jordan said the account surprised him because researchers he encountered at the time generally treated alleged abductions as experiences that could not simply be stopped once they had begun.

He said he later collected other testimonies from people who reported that prayer, hymns or appeals to Jesus appeared to end similar experiences. Jordan has said those accounts strengthened his Christian beliefs and led him to see what he described as the 'power' and 'authority' of Jesus Christ.

The accounts remain personal testimony rather than independently verified evidence. They do not establish that physical abductions occurred, that extraterrestrial beings were involved or that invoking a religious name caused the reported experiences to end.

Jordan's CE4 Research Group website says the organisation has worked with more than 600 alleged abduction cases. Jordan, however, said in a July 2026 interview that he had handled 'well over 700' case histories since 1997.

The difference means the higher figure is best treated as Jordan's more recent personal estimate rather than an independently confirmed total.

UFO Investigator Reframes Alien Claims as Spiritual Experiences

Jordan says his interpretation of the reports changed over time. Rather than viewing the alleged encounters as evidence that people were physically taken by extraterrestrial beings, he came to regard at least some of them as spiritual experiences.

'Nobody's getting taken anywhere,' Jordan said in one recent account of his views. He described the phenomenon as 'a demonic vision' and a 'demonic spiritual visionary experience.'

That description is Jordan's religious interpretation of testimony he has collected, not a scientifically established explanation.

Jordan has also claimed that involvement in occult or paranormal practices can, in his view, leave people more vulnerable to such episodes.

He has pointed to terms such as 'interdimensional,' 'extradimensional' and 'ultradimensional,' which have appeared in discussions of unexplained phenomena, as consistent with his view that the experiences may not involve visitors travelling from another planet.

Jordan's conclusions therefore rest primarily on witness accounts and his interpretation of them. The testimonies may explain why his beliefs changed, but they do not independently establish what caused the experiences he described.

For Jordan, the recurring reports of prayers or appeals to Jesus became the central feature of his research. For readers, however, the distinction remains important: the documented fact is that people reported these experiences and that Jordan drew a religious conclusion from them, not that an extraterrestrial or supernatural cause has been proven.
